attribution.note: Zitron wrote this sentence in his own essay and endorses it. It is not a quotation of anyone else.

semantics.note: Firm wording ('requires', 'will continue... in perpetuity'). It combines a present claim with an indefinite forecast. The normalisation keeps both parts and the perpetual horizon.

contract.note: The speaker gave no unit and no comparison set. Reading this as total organisation-wide compute compared with every other organisation is an ordinary plain reading. The result depends on how 'anyone' and 'needed' are read, and the contract flags this correctly.

evidence.note: Epoch AI, an independent source, published this before the evaluation date. Its year-end 2025 estimates put OpenAI narrowly ahead of DeepMind on median compute, but the uncertainty ranges overlap and only leading labs are covered. It shows no verified loss of the lead and does not show a historical maximum.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was stated. The evidence neither establishes the claimed maximum compute requirement nor shows a verified loss of it. Epoch's estimates for leading labs overlap with DeepMind and do not cover all organisations or unmet demand. The early-resolution rule is not met, and a finite lead can never prove perpetuity.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his essay. He endorses them with the follow-up 'It is that simple.'

semantics.note: A firm conditional ('will collapse'). The antecedent, that OpenAI cannot fulfil its obligations, is preserved. No horizon was stated.

contract.note: Defining collapse as insolvency, a distress restructuring or cessation of business is a fair ordinary reading. The trigger is tied to OpenAI's obligations to CoreWeave, which matches the surrounding passage.

evidence.note: CoreWeave's June 2026 10-Q is a company disclosure. It lists OpenAI as a significant customer and describes non-payment only as a risk. It does not document any OpenAI default, so the antecedent is not shown to have occurred.

reviews.rationale: The antecedent, OpenAI being unable to meet its obligations to CoreWeave, is not documented in the evidence available by the cutoff. Its status is unknown, so the conditional forecast is not scored. The consequence cannot be assessed until a qualifying default is established.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his essay, stated as fact.

semantics.note: A universal factual claim with an NVIDIA exception, plus losses of billions at three named companies. The normalisation captures both. It omits his remark that he could not find a profitable software company, which is acceptable because that remark is part of the same assertion.

contract.note: Choosing 2024 annual results and treating 'billions' as at least $2bn each is an ordinary reading. The speaker named no accounting basis: CoreWeave's net loss falls short of billions, but cash burn could exceed it. The contract rightly says the basis decides the result.

evidence.note: Kiplinger reports CoreWeave's 2024 net loss of $863M, citing the S-1. That is below billions on a net-loss reading, but the speaker's accounting basis is unspecified, so this item is not decisive under the contract.
CNBC, published before the evaluation date, reports that OpenAI lost about $5bn in 2024. This matches the OpenAI part, but the loss measure is undefined and it says nothing about the universal claim.
The Midjourney founder said in 2022 that the company was profitable. That is a different period from the 2024 target, so it is context only.

reviews.rationale: The OpenAI loss of about $5bn fits. CoreWeave's 2024 net loss of $863M falls short of billions, but the speaker gave no accounting basis, and the contract requires one before scoring. Anthropic's 2024 loss is not established. Profitable non-NVIDIA firms in 2024 are not ruled out either, since the Midjourney evidence is from 2022. The universal claim cannot be settled on this packet.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his essay. 'As I've written before' signals that he endorses it.

semantics.note: A factual observation with a numeric threshold: the nearest competitor has under 5% of ChatGPT's 500M weekly users, i.e. under 25M. The normalisation preserves this.

contract.note: Using the latest month before publication and testing the 25M weekly ceiling with the speaker's own 500M base is fair. Using daily users as a lower bound on weekly users is mathematically valid for the same population.

evidence.note: NPR reporting of Google's court documents gives Gemini 35M daily users in March 2025. Weekly users must be at least that, so Gemini had at least 35M, above the 25M ceiling. The same documents rank Meta AI above Gemini.

reviews.rationale: Google's measurements, presented in court and reported by NPR, show Gemini at 35M daily active users in March 2025. Weekly users must be at least as many as daily users, so Gemini had at least 35M weekly users. That is 7% of the claimed 500M base, above the 5% ceiling. Meta AI reportedly ranked even higher. The claimed under-5% gap is false for the target period.
